prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on what kind of coverage you need (individual/family, small‑group, Medicare, Medicaid), whether you want in‑person help, and which side of Kansas City you live on (Missouri vs Kansas). I can help you find someone, but here are practical steps and tips so you pick a good local broker.

How to find reputable brokers in Kansas City
- Use official directories
  - National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) “Find an Agent” tool.
  - Your state insurance department (Missouri or Kansas) to confirm licenses and check complaint history.
  - HealthCare.gov (for ACA marketplace) lists certified agents/navigators for open enrollment.
  - Medicare.gov / State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) for free, unbiased Medicare counseling.
- Check local reviews and references
  - Google, Yelp, and the Better Business Bureau for ratings and complaint patterns.
  - Ask friends, family, employers, or local HR groups for recommendations.

Questions to ask any broker before you hire them
- Are you licensed in Missouri and/or Kansas? (Make them show license info.)
- Are you independent or captive (do you only sell one carrier’s plans)?
- Which carriers and plan types do you represent?
- How are you paid — commission, fee, or both? Will payment affect your recommendations?
- Do you assist with enrollments, claims issues, and year‑round service?
- Can you provide references from current Kansas City clients?
- Do you have experience helping people in my situation (age, health needs, Medicare, small business)?

Red flags
- Refuses to disclose licensing or how they’re paid.
- Pushes only one insurer without explaining why.
- Makes guarantees about specific benefits or claim outcomes.
- High pressure to sign immediately.

If you’re shopping for Medicare specifically
- Use a licensed Medicare broker or SHIP counselor (free).
- Confirm the broker is contracted with the carriers you’re considering and has experience with Medicare Advantage vs. Medigap.

If you want, I can:
- Look up licensed brokers near you if you give your ZIP code and tell me whether you need individual/family, small group, or Medicare help.
- Draft an email/phone script you can use when contacting brokers.
